references.text: "Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity!" In [ref:Ps 6:9|Psalm 6:9], David uses almost the same wording that Jesus quotes here: "Go away from me, all you who do evil" (ἀπόστητε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ πάντες ἐργάται ἀδικίας). Jesus applies David's words as an eschatological judgment on those who do not know him.

In [ref:Matt 7:22-23|Matthew 7:22-23], we find a parallel to this verse in the Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus says: "I never knew you. Depart from me, you workers of iniquity!" Both texts deal with people who claim a relationship with Jesus but whom he rejects on the day of judgment.

In the parable of the ten virgins, the bridegroom says in [ref:Matt 25:12|Matthew 25:12]: "Truly, I say to you, I do not know you." The same motif appears in Luke 13:27 – the Lord refuses to recognize those who were not prepared.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 13:25-26|Luke 13:25-26] shows that the master of the house first shuts the door and then says "I do not know where you come from" to those knocking. Verse 27 repeats and reinforces this rejection with the addition to depart.

In [ref:2 Tim 2:19|2 Timothy 2:19], Paul quotes: "The Lord knows those who are his," and "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity (ἀδικίας)." This text links the theme that the Lord knows his own with the idea that unrighteousness (ἀδικία) is incompatible with belonging to him – the same theme found in Luke 13:27.

In [ref:Luk 6:46|Luke 6:46], Jesus asks: "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and not do what I say?" This sheds light on the background of the rejection in 13:27 – those who confess Jesus with their mouths but do not live in obedience will be rejected.
In [ref:Matt 25:41|Matthew 25:41], the king says to those on his left: "Depart from me, you cursed." The same pattern of final rejection from the Lord's presence as in Luke 13:27.

In [ref:Sal 1:6|Psalm 1:6] it is written that "The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish." The theme that the Lord knows (or does not know) people's ways underlies Jesus' words in Luke 13:27 about not knowing where they come from.
